item.title: Lowering the Cost of Curiosity
item.description:
I have been doing a lot of experimentation with local models recently, as have many of my colleagues. There is also a growing anticipation around the next generation of developer workstations and AI-focused boxes: machines capable of running increasingly useful models without sending every request to a SaaS platform.

It is easy to see this as another technology choice: local versus cloud, open model versus proprietary model, workstation versus API. I think the more interesting question for enterprises is economic.

item.title: When Trust Becomes the Constraint
item.description:
One of the more difficult problems I keep coming back to with AI-assisted software modernisation isn’t really a technology problem. It’s trust.

We have all seen an LLM confidently make something up, merge two facts that happened to look similar, or produce an explanation that sounds entirely reasonable until someone who really understands the domain reads it. Once you have seen that happen a few times, it changes how you approach the capability, and that matters when we start asking AI to help modernise software.
